newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Life pension sales out of proportion - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Life pension sales out of proportion - MOF.

text.p: Sales of pensions for individuals at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co were out of proportion to those of other companies, and this contributed to a chronic worsening of its business, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Friday.

Nissan Life, which was ordered to shut down operations except for servicing of current customers on Friday morning, had to keep paying high returns for products sold to individuals, which promised a life-long payment, said Makoto Fukuda, director of the insurance department at the ministry's banking bureau.

Of its total assets of more than two trillion yen, pensions for individuals accounted for 1.01 trillion yen, or about 49 percent. The average share of pensions among all insurance firms is about seven percent, he said.
